questions.q: What's the key difference between the Internet and the World Wide Web?
options: The Internet is the physical infrastructure (cables, routers, servers); the Web is the information/services that travel on it
They're the same thing, just different names
The Web is the hardware; the Internet is the software
The Internet only carries email; the Web carries everything else

questions.q: Who invented the World Wide Web, and where?
options: Bill Gates, at Microsoft
Tim Berners-Lee, at CERN in Switzerland
Steve Jobs, at Apple
The U.S. military, at the Pentagon

questions.q: What is an intranet?
options: A faster version of the internet
A restricted, internal network only for members of a specific group (like a hospital's internal system)
The original name for the World Wide Web
A backup internet used when the main one goes down

questions.q: What does DNS actually do?
options: It encrypts data between browser and server
It connects human-friendly domain names to the numerical IP addresses computers use
It designs the visual layout of a website
It compresses images for faster loading

questions.q: In the client-server relationship, what is the "client"?
options: The company paying for the website
The web server storing the files
Your web browser, which requests pages from a server
The domain registrar

questions.q: What does a DNS record's TTL (Time to Live) control?
options: How long a website stays online before it must be renewed
How long other servers may cache (hold onto) a DNS answer before checking again
How fast a page loads
How long a domain name can be

questions.q: In the URL https://www.pixelpaws.com/products/collars?type=nylon, what is "pixelpaws.com"?
options: The protocol
The domain name
The query parameter
The path

questions.q: What does the "S" in HTTPS actually mean for your data?
options: It means the site was Specially approved by Google
It means the connection between your browser and the server is encrypted
It means the site loads Slower but Safer
It means the site is Sponsored content

questions.q: What role does a Certificate Authority (CA) play in HTTPS?
options: It hosts the actual website files
It signs and verifies a server's SSL certificate so browsers can trust it
It registers the domain name
It writes the website's code

questions.q: What is the 60-30-10 rule used for?
options: Splitting a webpage's load time across three servers
Balancing a color palette: 60% dominant color, 30% secondary, 10% accent
Setting font sizes for headings
Deciding image compression ratios

questions.q: According to the reading, about how long does it take a user to understand a page's purpose without reading any text?
options: 3-5 seconds
30 seconds
1 minute
Instantly, in under a second

questions.q: What's the main difference between an F-pattern and a Z-pattern layout?
options: F-pattern is for content-heavy pages; Z-pattern is for simple pages with a clear focal path
F-pattern is only used on mobile; Z-pattern only on desktop
They are the same pattern with different names
F-pattern uses color; Z-pattern uses only grayscale

ch1_lab_know_your_guild.title: Quick Check: CTSOs & the Perkins Act

questions.q: What does CTSO stand for?
options: Career and Technical Student Organization
Computer Technology Student Organization
Certified Training and Skills Office
Career Technical Support Office

questions.q: What federal law funds and requires programs like this one, including CTSO participation?
options: The No Child Left Behind Act
The Carl D. Perkins Career and Technical Education Act
The Individuals with Disabilities Education Act
The Every Student Succeeds Act

questions.q: According to the SkillsUSA Framework, Technical Skills make up roughly what share of the three-part framework?
options: All of it - it's the only part that matters
Two-thirds
One-third, alongside Personal Skills and Workplace Skills
None - it's purely soft skills

questions.q: What set of rules is most commonly used to run formal meetings fairly, and who wrote it?
options: Robert's Rules of Order, written by Henry Martyn Robert
The Perkins Act, written by Congress
The SkillsUSA Code, written by the U.S. Department of Education
The Meeting Manual, written by FBLA

questions.q: What does "seconding" a motion actually mean?
options: It means the person agrees with the motion
It means the motion gets voted on twice
It just keeps the motion alive for discussion - it doesn't mean agreement
It means the motion automatically passes

questions.q: What's the difference between a Standing Committee and an Ad Hoc Committee?
options: Standing committees are permanent; Ad Hoc committees are temporary, formed for one specific purpose
Standing committees meet while standing up; Ad Hoc committees sit down
There is no real difference
Ad Hoc committees are always larger than Standing committees

questions.q: What makes something "service learning" instead of just volunteering?
options: It has to involve money changing hands
It's directly tied to class learning and requires structured reflection, not just helping out
It has to happen on a weekend
It's the exact same thing as volunteering

questions.q: On the Work-Based Learning ladder, which tier involves actually doing paid, structured work (like Cooperative Education or Apprenticeship)?
options: Awareness
Exploration
Application
Observation

questions.q: What does "pro bono" work mean for a design agency, according to the reading?
options: Work done for free that's purely charity, not smart business
Free professional work for non-profits that builds portfolio and generates referrals - smart business, not just charity
Work that's illegal to charge for
A discount given only to friends and family

questions.q: According to the dress code levels, when are you required to wear the SkillsUSA Official Uniform?
options: Every day of class
For ALL SkillsUSA competitions and events, no exceptions
Only during job interviews
Never - it's optional

questions.q: What's the "golden rule" given for when you're not sure how to dress for a professional situation?
options: Wear whatever is most comfortable
When in doubt, go more formal
Always match what your classmates are wearing
Ask a stranger for advice

questions.q: What's the approximate starting salary range for an entry-level developer in Nevada, per the reading?
options: $10/hour part-time only

questions.q: Why is the answer "I'm a hard worker" considered weak in an interview, per the reading?
options: It's grammatically incorrect
It's vague and gives the interviewer no specific evidence, unlike a story with a real example
Interviewers don't want to hear about work ethic at all
It's too long an answer

questions.q: What do interviewers actually evaluate beyond technical skill, according to the reading?
options: Only your grades
Your communication, professionalism, and ability to give specific, evidence-based answers
Only how you're dressed
Nothing else matters besides coding ability

questions.q: Which of these is one of the 8 standard interview questions covered in the reading?
options: What's your favorite color?
Tell me about a time you worked as part of a team
How many followers do you have on social media?
What's your home address?

questions.q: What is a "career pathway," as defined in the reading?
options: A single required class
A formal, intentional sequence of courses that moves you from student to professional
A physical hallway in the school
A list of job interview questions

questions.q: Per the BLS salary data cited in the reading, which role has the highest projected growth rate?
options: Web Developer at +16%
UI/UX Designer at +13%
Full-Stack Developer at +25%
Freelance Web Designer at +5%

questions.q: Why does the reading warn against typing an email in ALL CAPS?
options: It's harder to read on mobile devices
Because it reads as yelling, even if that's not the intent
It takes longer to type
It's against school policy to use capital letters

questions.q: According to the Project Triangle, if a client wants a project done Fast and Good, what does that mean for cost?
options: It will be cheap
It will be Expensive
Cost doesn't matter in the Project Triangle
It will be free

questions.q: What is a Minimum Viable Product (MVP)?
options: The cheapest possible product regardless of quality
A version of a product with just enough features to be usable, so early customers can give feedback
The final, fully polished version of a product
A product with no features at all

questions.q: What does the "Critique Sandwich" structure look like when giving feedback?
options: Criticism, criticism, criticism
Positive comment, then the criticism, then another positive comment
Only positive comments, never criticism
A written report with no spoken conversation

questions.q: What must your homepage file always be named?
options: home.html
index.html, all lowercase
Homepage.html
main.html or Main.html, either works

questions.q: Why does capitalization matter in file names for a real web server?
options: It doesn't matter at all
Linux servers are case-sensitive, so About.html and about.html are treated as two different files
Capital letters make files load faster
Servers automatically convert everything to lowercase anyway

questions.q: What should you use instead of a space in a file or folder name?
options: An underscore only, never anything else
A hyphen (-)
A period
Spaces are actually fine to use
